rules.title: Official Rules
rules.empty: No rules set yet. An admin can add them under Settings.
rules.gameText: Try the rules against an opponent: rock-paper-scissors, two throws per round, bombs, islands and everything else.
rules.sectionsHint: The house rules apply to every game, including the minigame.

sections.title: Basics
items: **Ten cups** per side, set up as a triangle. Played 1 vs 1 or in teams (2 vs 2).
**Who starts** is decided by a rock-paper-scissors duel. The winner starts.
**Two throws per round.** Then it is the other side's turn. Hit cups are only removed at the end of the round.

**Balls back:** If you sink **both balls** in a round, you get them back and may **throw two more**. That goes on until you no longer hit both. Every sunk ball counts, including one from a trick shot.
**Your elbow stays behind the edge of the table.** Otherwise the throw is void.

sections.title: Hits and special throws
items: **Bomb:** If both throws of a round land in the same cup, **three cups** are removed. Both balls went in, so you also get **balls back**.
**Island and bomb together:** Hit an island and then the same cup again with your second ball, and both add up: **five cups** (two for the island, three for the bomb).

**Island:** A cup counts as an island when **nothing is left around it**, for example the tip once the row behind it is gone: one cup of space to the next one. Then you can call "island". Hit it and **two cups** are gone. Hit an island with **two throws directly in a row** and the second one is **six cups**.
**Only two islands per game:** Everyone may call island twice at most. That holds for the whole game, including redemption and overtime. There are no new ones there, only unused ones.

**Bounce:** If the ball bounces on the table first and then lands in the cup, the hit counts **double**. A bounce may be stopped by swatting it away after it has bounced. There are no bounces in duels, because the other player is not at the table and could not swat. Swatting can knock one of your own cups over; it then stays gone. If the second ball then lands in the same cup (bomb), **four cups** are removed. If **both balls are bounces** into the same cup, it is **five cups**.

**Trick shot:** If the ball bounces off a cup and rolls back at least past the middle of the table, you may try a trick shot, for example with your eyes closed, under your leg or off the ceiling. This also applies to a **bounce shot** that glances off a cup and rolls back.
**Rolling over cups:** If the ball rolls over cups, the cups whose rim it rolled over do **not** count.

sections.title: Rearranging cups
items: Once only **four cups** are left on your opponent's side, the ones you have to hit, you may rearrange them **yourself**. It does not happen automatically, you do it.
You may only move them **onto the ten places** of the ten-cup setup, where a cup stands at the start. Not freely on the table.

You may rearrange **at the start of your round**, not in the middle: if five cups stand and you hit the first, the others must stay (it could still become a bomb). You rearrange the next time it is your turn. **Not after balls back:** If you sink both balls you throw again, but that is still the same turn. You may rearrange only once it is really your turn again after your opponent's.
**Each player** may rearrange **only once per game**. This also works **at the start of your redemption turn** if you have not done it yet.

sections.title: The end of a game
items: **Redemption:** If the player who started hits the last cup, **only the one who did not start** may catch up **once**. It is a single turn that only continues with balls back.

**Overtime:** If they hit all remaining cups, nothing is left on either side. The **front three cups per side** are set up again and play continues until someone wins. That repeats as often as needed. In the mini game duel each player plays the overtime separately: whoever is playing clears their three cups alone, then the other one has to answer. If both clear, the next overtime follows.
If the player who did not start is the first to hit all cups, they win right away.

sections.title: Penalties and fun
items: **Strip cup:** Only your **first hit** of the game counts: if it is the **middle cup of the third row from the front**, you have to stand at the table in your underwear. This applies to each player on their own. You may dress again with your next hit.
**Naked mile:** Whoever loses a whole game without hitting a single cup runs a lap around the block naked. It never happens, but it is funny anyway.

sections.title: Mini game in the app
items: **Duel:** One player goes first and plays alone until all cups are gone. Their throws are recorded. The other one answers whenever they have time and plays against exactly these throws. Rock, paper, scissors has already decided who starts.
**Accepted means started:** If you accept a duel and then leave it (the cross at the top right, reloading the page, closing the app), you have given up and lost. It cannot be started again.

**Overtime in a duel:** If both clear the table, each plays the three cups on their own, taking turns, until it is decided. There is no rearranging and no island call in overtime. An overtime cannot be declined.
**There are no bounce shots in a duel**, because the other player is not at the table and could not swat them away.

**Against the computer:** You may swat bounce shots away, and the computer swats yours. One of your own cups can go flying in the process. When the computer rearranges, it always uses 1-1-2: the tip, the middle of the third row and the two middle cups of the last row.

sections.title: Fair play
items: If you knock over the opponent's cups in front of you by accident, for example while swatting a bounce, **they stay gone**. Your own fault.
You may **not blow into** or **reach into** hit cups to get a spinning ball out and prevent the hit.
